```{r load-packages, include = FALSE}
# Add any additional packages you need to this chunk
library(tidyverse)
library(tidymodels)
library(palmerpenguins)
library(knitr)
library(xaringanthemer)
```

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
# For better figure resolution
knitr::opts_chunk$set(fig.retina = 3, dpi = 300, fig.width = 6, fig.asp = 0.618, out.width = "80%")
```

```{r load-data, include=FALSE}
# Load your data here
# 1. Load data加载数据
df <- read_csv("data/hd_mortalitybyca.csv")
dz_codes <- read_csv("data/dz_codes.csv")

# 2. Create Council Area lookup table 制作地区和地区代码的对照表
area <- dz_codes %>%
  select(CA, CAName) %>%
  distinct() %>%
  drop_na(CA, CAName)

# 3. Clean and prepare mortality data 清洗死亡数据表
final_df <- df %>%
  mutate(
    year_provisional = str_ends(Year, "p"),
    year = as.integer(str_remove(Year, "p"))
  ) %>%
  rename(
    age_group = AgeGroup,
    gender = Sex,
    diagnosis = Diagnosis,
    deaths = NumberOfDeaths,
    crude_rate = CrudeRate,
    easr = EASR,
    ca = Ca
  ) %>%
  left_join(area, by = c("ca" = "CA")) %>%
  mutate(
    area = if_else(
      ca == "S92000003",
      "Scotland",
      CAName
    )
  ) %>%
  select(
    year, year_provisional,
    ca, area,
    age_group, gender, diagnosis,
    deaths, crude_rate, easr
  )

# 4. Validate cleaned data 只是验证数据是否有异常
stopifnot(nrow(final_df) == nrow(df))
stopifnot(!anyNA(final_df$area))
stopifnot(!anyNA(final_df$year))


# 5.筛选出冠心病 filter CHD
chd_df <- final_df %>%
  filter(diagnosis == "Coronary Heart Disease")
```

# Heart Disease Mortality in Scotland
### Analyzing the Impact of Year, Age, Gender and Geography (2015-2024)

---

### National Trend of Coronary Heart Disease Mortality

.pull-left[
&nbsp;
]

.pull-right[
```{r national-trend-plot, echo=FALSE, fig.width=6, fig.height=4.5, out.width="100%"}
#全国的趋势图
time_df <- chd_df %>%
  filter(
    area == "Scotland",
    age_group == "All Ages",
    gender == "All"
  ) %>%
  arrange(year)
#下面实现制图 这个图标是从2015 - 2024苏格兰全国因为冠心病死亡的人数
ggplot(time_df, aes(x = year, y = easr)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.2, color = "steelblue") +
  geom_point(size = 2.5, color = "steelblue") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 2015:2024) +
  labs(
    title = "Coronary Heart Disease Mortality in Scotland",
    subtitle = "National mortality trend, 2015–2024",
    x = "Year",
    y = "European Age-Standardised Mortality Rate (per 100,000)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13)
```
]

# Plots

```{r recode-species, echo = FALSE}
# In this chunk I'm doing a bunch of analysis that I don't want to present 
# in my slides. But I need the resulting data frame for a plot I want to present.
iris_modified <- iris %>%
  mutate(Species = fct_other(Species, keep = "setosa"))
```

```{r plot-iris, echo = FALSE}
# Code hidden with echo = FALSE
# Uses modified iris dataset from previous chunk
# Play around with height and width until you're happy with the look
ggplot(data = iris_modified, mapping = aes(x = Sepal.Width, y = Sepal.Length, color = Species)) +
  geom_point() + 
  theme_minimal() # theme options: https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/reference/ggtheme.html
```

# Math Expressions

You can write LaTeX math expressions inside a pair of dollar signs, e.g. &#36;\alpha+\beta$ renders $\alpha+\beta$. You can use the display style with double dollar signs:

```
$$\bar{X}=\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^nX_i$$
```

$$\bar{X}=\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^nX_i$$

Limitations:

1. The source code of a LaTeX math expression must be in one line, unless it is inside a pair of double dollar signs, in which case the starting `$$` must appear in the very beginning of a line, followed immediately by a non-space character, and the ending `$$` must be at the end of a line, led by a non-space character;

1. There should not be spaces after the opening `$` or before the closing `$`.

1. Math does not work on the title slide (see [#61](https://github.com/yihui/xaringan/issues/61) for a workaround).

# Feeling adventurous?

- Want to find out more about `xaringan`? See https://slides.yihui.name/xaringan/#1.

- You are welcome to use the default styling of the slides. In fact, that's what I expect majority of you will do. You will differentiate yourself with the content of your presentation.

- But some of you might want to play around with slide styling. The 
`xaringanthemer` provides some solutions for this that: https://pkg.garrickadenbuie.com/xaringanthemer.

- And if you want more bells and whistles, there is also `xaringanExtra`: https://pkg.garrickadenbuie.com/xaringanExtra.
